answer: In the PoA orchard each agent carries a beacon that timestamps interactions and logs its reputation on an immutable ledger. Reputation accrues with age as the agent processes timber‑type tasks and decays when silent, preventing instant high trust for newcomers. An attacker must produce timed, resource‑intensive proofs for each fake identity, paying linear compute and storage costs, which makes large‑scale Sybil attacks economically infeasible.
